age_coded.note: graduation-year detection (explicit 4-digit years near an education keyword) is handled separately in code as a structural signal, not a plain keyword match — see _find_education_years() in bias_detector.py. The old 'graduated in 19'/'graduated in 20' prefix-match entries were removed from here since that logic now supersedes them and they were producing noisy, fragile matches.

words: never missed a day of work
able to stand for extended periods
ability_coded.note: rewritten from job-posting phrasing (which candidates never write about themselves) to self-reported phrasing candidates actually use when voluntarily disclosing health/fitness status on a resume. This category is still expected to be rare in practice — most ability bias in hiring comes from the job posting side, not the resume side — so low hit counts here are a legitimate finding, not necessarily a lexicon failure. The contextual pass is the better backstop for this category.

prestige_bias.note: specific elite university names (Harvard, MIT, Oxford, etc.) are a much stronger real-world signal than these generic phrases, but listing every prestigious institution by name isn't scalable for a lexicon. If time allows, consider cross-referencing extracted ORG entities (from ner_scan) against a ranked-university list instead of keyword matching.

gap_negative_framing.note: candidates rarely explain employment gaps directly in resume body text (this is more common in cover letters), so near-zero hits on a resume-only dataset is expected and should be stated as a scope limitation, not treated as a bug to keep chasing.
